newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - Brazilian differentials ease.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - Brazilian differentials ease.

text.p: Brazilian spreads showed some signs of softening this week on the New York physical coffee market, but spot business remained exceedingly slow, traders said.
"There is very little going on in physicals," said a trader. "Brazils are easing because the crop is starting to come in and quality is not that good. It's too wild."

Heavy rainfall in Brazil's key coffee growing regions during June -- in the midst of the 1997/98 harvest -- spoiled the cup quality, he said. "They look and taste like they were prematurely harvested," the trader said.
Spot Santos 4s were offered at 12-13 cents under the CSCE September contract, a cent or two easier than week ago levels. Spot Santos 2/3s netted two-to-four cents under "C".

Most other differentials, however, were fairly steady on the week. Spot Colombians MAMs held firm at 25 cents over "C", although some dealers said they had heard of slightly lower offers earlier in the week. A small quantity of Supremos, also on the spot market, garnered some 40 cents over "C".
Colombians forward delivery continued to attract more interest, with Colombians for October-December shipment fetching 22 to 23 cents over the CSCE December contract.
Traders noted increasing demand from European trade houses for Central American beans for early autumn delivery, but no prices were quoted.
CSCE September coffee rose 3.85 cents a lb Friday to settle at 164.30. December ended 2.50 cents higher at 150.10.
